subsystems.name: Power source
subsystems.role: provides the energy needed to melt regolith particles.
parts: energy storage (batteries or regenerative fuel cells)

subsystems.name: Regolith handling
subsystems.role: excavates, transports and prepares raw moon or Mars dust.

subsystems.name: Sintering head
subsystems.role: concentrates thermal energy onto the regolith surface to fuse it.

subsystems.name: Motion and positioning
subsystems.role: moves the sintering head across the build area with millimetre precision.

subsystems.name: Control and monitoring
subsystems.role: regulates beam power, scan speed and layer thickness to avoid cracks.

subsystems.name: Dust and thermal management
subsystems.role: contains loose regolith and manages heat in a vacuum.

buildSteps.title: Survey and select the site
buildSteps.detail: Map the regolith composition and thickness, and choose a flat area with material rich in iron, titanium or other phases that absorb the chosen energy efficiently.

buildSteps.title: Excavate the regolith
buildSteps.detail: A robotic scoop or bucket wheel digs up the top few centimetres to a few tens of centimetres of dust and broken rock.

buildSteps.title: Sieve and condition the material
buildSteps.detail: Remove large rocks and, if needed, heat the regolith in a sealed container to drive off volatiles that could cause bubbles or poor bonding.

buildSteps.title: Deposit a uniform layer
buildSteps.detail: Spread the sieved regolith to a controlled thickness — typically a few millimetres to a few centimetres — using a hopper or blade.

buildSteps.title: Sinter the layer
buildSteps.detail: Scan a laser, microwave beam or concentrated sunlight across the surface. The particles melt at their contact points and fuse into a ceramic-like solid.

buildSteps.title: Build up or move on
buildSteps.detail: Either deposit and sinter layer upon layer to make a three-dimensional shape, or sinter continuous strips side by side to pave a large area.

buildSteps.title: Cool and inspect
buildSteps.detail: Let the structure cool slowly to avoid thermal cracking. Cameras and thermal sensors check for gaps, warping or incomplete fusion.

buildSteps.title: Finish or assemble
buildSteps.detail: If making blocks, stack them into walls or arches. If building in place, add loose regolith on top as extra radiation shielding.

prerequisites.why: Earth-based mining and robotic digging are mature, but no system has yet operated extensively on the Moon or Mars.
Solar arrays work in sunlight, but lunar nights last about 14 Earth days; nuclear surface power is still in prototype testing.
Robotic arms and rovers exist, but fully autonomous site preparation, deposition and sintering without human tending has not been demonstrated.
Lasers and microwaves operate in vacuum, but designs must survive abrasive dust, extreme temperature swings and thermal cycling.
Spacecraft routinely manage heat by radiation only; this knowledge transfers directly to sintering equipment.

prerequisites.tech: Lunar and Martian regolith simulants and process models
prerequisites.why: Simulants exist on Earth, but their particle size and mineralogy differ from real regolith, so results must be validated on site.

pathway.milestone: Laboratory experiments sinter small tiles and bricks from lunar and Martian simulants using lasers, microwaves and solar concentrators.
pathway.unlocks: Basic process parameters — power, scan speed, layer thickness — and proof that sintering can produce strong solids in vacuum.

pathway.milestone: A robotic payload on a lunar lander demonstrates sintering a small patch of real regolith under actual vacuum and temperature cycling.
pathway.unlocks: Confidence that hardware survives launch, landing and the lunar environment, and real data on dust behaviour.

pathway.milestone: Robotic construction of a landing pad or a simple shelter from sintered regolith.
pathway.unlocks: Dust-free landing zones and rudimentary protective structures, reducing the cost of later missions.

pathway.milestone: Human habitats built partly or wholly from sintered regolith, covered with loose regolith for radiation shielding.
pathway.unlocks: Sustainable bases that use local materials instead of importing every structural element from Earth.
